expected_behavior: Any uncommitted change makes a real revert refuse with exit 1 before touching anything; a dry run still previews and says the tree must be clean first.
--dry-run prints a JSON plan and creates no revert commit, so the impact is shown before the action.
A revert runs only after the user approved the exact commits the dry run listed; without a terminal the script refuses unless --yes comes with --expect-sha naming those commits.
--last 1 targets the most recent commit, and --last N the N most recent, newest first; a merge commit needs --mainline.
Each reverted commit gets its own conventional revert commit made through o-commit's script, with no shell in between.
